results.title: Allowances - Fair Work Ombudsman
results.description:
# Allowances
Employees may be entitled to allowances for doing certain tasks, working in certain locations, using a special skill or for incurring expenses for doing their job. Find out what applies to you.

## What is an allowance?
Allowances are extra payments made to employees who:

- do certain tasks
- have a particular skill they use at work
- use their own tools at work
- work in unpleasant or hazardous conditions
- incur an expense for doing their job.

Common allowances include:

- uniforms and special clothing
- tools and equipment
- travel and fares
- car and phone
- first-aid
- leading hand or supervisor
- industry of employment (for example building and construction).

## Calculating allowances
The allowances that you or your employees are entitled to will depend on the award that applies. Use our [Pay and Conditions Tool](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/pay-and-wages/pay-calculator) to find the allowances that apply in your industry.

You can also check out our downloadable [pay guides](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/pay-and-wages/minimum-wages/pay-guides) for allowances in your industry.

If you're covered by an agreement, your allowances will be in your agreement. To find an enterprise agreement, go to the [Fair Work Commission](https://www.fwc.gov.au/work-conditions/enterprise-agreements/find-enterprise-agreement) website.

## Workplace arrangements affecting allowances
- [annualised wages](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/pay-and-wages/minimum-wages/annualised-wages-and-salaries)
- [employment contracts](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/employment-contracts/about-employment-contracts)
- [Individual flexibility arrangements (IFAs)](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/flexibility-in-the-workplace/individual-flexibility-arrangements)
- a [guarantee of annual earningsA written arrangement that allows an employer to pay an employee the high income threshold or higher, over 12 months or more. The employee will not receive entitlements from a relevant award.](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/taxonomy/term/420).

The wages salary payments, employment contracts, IFAs and guarantees of annual earnings need to compensate for other penalties and loadings in an applicable award.

## Related information
**Tip: Help for employees and employers**

Problems can happen in any workplace. If you’ve got a workplace problem, we have information, tools and resources to help you.

Learn more at [Workplace problems](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/workplace-problems).

# Modern Awards
## What Is A Modern Award?
Entitlements set out in the modern award include pay, hours of work, [overtime rates](https://employsure.com.au/guides/wage-and-pay/overtime-rates), [penalty rates](https://employsure.com.au/guides/wage-and-pay/penalty-rates), allowances, rosters, breaks and leave entitlements specific to the industry or occupation.

- Maximum weekly hours

## Your Employment Obligations
For example, if a physiotherapist is hired straight after graduating from university, their minimum award pay rate will be lower than the applicable modern award rate for an employee with five years of experience.

## Frequently Asked Questions
- allowances

An employee can only be covered by one award with regards to their employment in a particular role.
